record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Is there an integer k such that 2-abelian squares of period at least k can be avoided over a binary alphabet?

evidence.quote: Is there a natural integer k such that 2-abelian-squares of period at least k can be avoided over a binary alphabet?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. For a positive integer $k$, two words $u,v \in \Sigma^*$ are said to be $k$-abelian equivalent, written $u \sim_k v$, if for every word $w \in \Sigma^*$ with $|w| \le k$, the number of occurrences of $w$ as a (contiguous) factor of $u$ equals the number of occurrences of $w$ as a factor of $v$. (For $k=1$ this is ordinary abelian equivalence; for $k \ge \max(|u|,|v|)$ it coincides with equality.)

A $k$-abelian square is a nonempty word of the form $uv$ with $|u| = |v|$ and $u \sim_k v$; the integer $|u|$ is called its period. An infinite word $\mathbf{w} \in \Sigma^{\mathbb{N}}$ is said to avoid $k$-abelian squares of period at least $p$ if no factor of $\mathbf{w}$ is a $k$-abelian square whose period is $\ge p$.

Question: Does there exist a positive integer $k$ such that there is an infinite word over the binary alphabet $\Sigma = \{0,1\}$ that avoids all $2$-abelian squares of period at least $k$?
artifact.status_search_result: The closest known result (Rao–Rosenfeld) shows that 3-abelian squares of period at least 3 can be avoided in an infinite binary word, but the analogous statement for 2-abelian squares over a binary alphabet does not appear to be established. No source found resolves the question for k=2 over the binary alphabet, and it is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions (Rao, Rosenfeld)
status_evidence.snippet: One can avoid 3-abelian-squares of period at least 3 in infinite binary words; 2-abelian-squares of period at least 2 are avoided in infinite ternary words.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results address 3-abelian squares on binary and 2-abelian squares on ternary, leaving the binary 2-abelian case open.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions, Math. Comp.
status_evidence.snippet: Results on k-abelian repetition avoidance over binary and ternary alphabets.
status_evidence.claim: Published version provides partial results but not the binary 2-abelian-square long-period avoidance.
